entities.description: A system where people in different locations are connected and see each other/things on a screen in real-time.

entities.name: SCREEN
entities.description: A display device used to view content, which aids interaction in a video conferencing system but does not create a virtual environment.

entities.name: VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT
entities.description: The first characteristic of a VR system where the user is surrounded by a computer-generated environment.

entities.name: REAL TIME
entities.description: The state of events happening immediately as they occur, which distinguishes video conferencing from a virtual environment.

entities.name: REAL WORLD ENVIRONMENT
entities.description: An environment that is physically real but viewed through a medium like a screen.

entities.name: IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE
entities.description: The second characteristic of a VR system involving the blocking of senses to feel present in a virtual world.

entities.name: INTERACTIVE
entities.description: The third characteristic of a VR system where the user is able to change or influence what is being displayed.

entities.name: VR SYSTEM
entities.description: A system characterized by three main requirements: a virtual environment, an immersive experience, and interactivity.

entities.name: 3D MOVIE
entities.description: A popular form of cinema where users wear glasses to see content in 3D, providing a virtual environment and semi-immersive experience.

entities.name: 3D GLASS
entities.description: A wearable device used by viewers to perceive 3D content in a movie.

entities.name: AUDITORIUM
entities.description: A physical location where people sit to watch a 3D movie.

entities.name: SEMI-IMMERSIVE
entities.description: A level of immersion that is partly achieved by blocking visual and auditory senses, as seen in 3D movies.

relationships.description: The system uses a screen to display the connection to other people.
The system functions in real time, which prevents it from being considered a virtual environment.
Virtual environment is the first required characteristic of a VR system.
Immersive experience is the second required characteristic of a VR system.
Interactivity is the third required characteristic of a VR system.
Users wear 3D glasses to watch a 3D movie.
A 3D movie provides a virtual environment to the viewer.
A 3D movie provides a semi-immersive experience because it partially blocks senses.
A 3D movie is identified as not being interactive because the user cannot change what is displayed.

entities.description: A phenomenon related to usability and acceptability in VR, characterized by three aspects: causes, evaluation, and mitigation.

entities.name: INTERNAL FACTORS
entities.description: A set of individual characteristics and conditions inherent to users that can contribute to an increased likelihood of experiencing cyber sickness.

entities.name: EXTERNAL FACTORS
entities.description: Factors external to the user that can cause cyber sickness, including hardware and VR content.

entities.name: HARDWARE
entities.description: A sub-factor of external factors that can cause cyber sickness.

entities.name: VR CONTENT
entities.description: A sub-factor of external factors that can cause cyber sickness; it can be categorized as general VR content or controllable content.

entities.name: AGE
entities.description: An internal factor where children (2-12 years) may exhibit increased sensitivity to cyber sickness, while older persons may experience higher levels; the relationship is more visible in controllable content.

entities.name: GENDER
entities.description: An internal factor whose impact on cyber sickness has been studied with inconclusive results, with some studies suggesting women may experience more severe cases.

entities.name: HEAD-MOUNTED DISPLAYS, HMDS
entities.description: A hardware device that, when used by females, is associated with an increase in cyber sickness.

Gender is cited as another internal factor contributing to cyber sickness.
Studies indicate a relationship between age and cyber sickness susceptibility.

Usage of HMDs by females is associated with an increase in cyber sickness.
The relationship between age and cyber sickness is more visible when viewing controllable content versus general VR content.

entities.description: The visual experience of perceiving depth, which is facilitated by the inter-pupillary distance and provided by VR displays.

entities.name: CYBERSICKNESS
entities.description: Also referred to as visually induced motion sickness (CS), it is a condition where users experience symptoms related to virtual reality usage, influenced by internal and external factors.

entities.name: PRIOR EXPOSURE
entities.description: One of the conditions that can satisfy a positive correlation regarding the onset of cybersickness.

entities.name: REPEATED EXPOSURE
entities.description: One of the conditions that can satisfy a positive correlation regarding the onset of cybersickness.

entities.name: PHYSICAL CONDITIONS
entities.description: An internal factor responsible for the induction or severity of cybersickness.

entities.name: BODY AWARENESS
entities.description: A specific physical condition defined as the ability of the user to attend to and perceive bodily sensations, which is an internal factor for CS.

entities.name: POOR SLEEP QUALITY
entities.description: A factor that may lead to, contribute to, or increase the severity of cybersickness.

entities.name: RETINAL ECCENTRICITY
entities.description: A physical attribute where people with greater retinal eccentricity may be more susceptible to cybersickness.

entities.name: MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS
entities.description: A neurological condition that may cause individuals to experience more severe cybersickness symptoms.

entities.name: PHYSICAL POSITION
entities.description: An internal factor where the posture of the user (e.g., standing vs. sitting) impacts susceptibility to and the onset of cybersickness.

entities.name: EMOTIONAL CONDITIONS
entities.description: Internal factors including emotions at the time of usage that affect the likelihood of experiencing cybersickness.

entities.name: NEGATIVE EMOTIONS
entities.description: Includes anxiety, stress, and frustration; these are typically associated with an increased likelihood of experiencing cybersickness.

entities.name: NEUROTICISM
entities.description: A personality trait that may increase the likelihood of experiencing cybersickness.

entities.name: AGE
entities.description: An internal factor related to the user's susceptibility to cybersickness.

entities.name: GENDER
entities.description: An internal factor related to the user's susceptibility to cybersickness.

entities.name: MOTION SICKNESS SUSCEPTIBILITY
entities.description: An internal factor regarding a user's inherent tendency to experience motion sickness.

entities.name: HARDWARE
entities.description: An external factor category that was initially thought to be the primary cause of cybersickness but is now seen as less fundamental than other aspects of devices.

entities.name: TECHNOLOGY
entities.description: The advancement of technology was once thought to eliminate cybersickness, but many problems remain despite technological progress.

entities.name: DEVICES
entities.description: Specific aspects of devices, regardless of how advanced they are, are responsible for inducing cybersickness.

entities.name: DISPLAY RESOLUTION
entities.description: A factor of devices where higher resolution leads to a better experience and reduced cybersickness up to a certain point.

entities.name: CYBERSICKNESS
entities.description: A physical discomfort or disorientation experienced by users in virtual environments, also referred to as CS.

entities.name: RESOLUTION
entities.description: A measure of image clarity in a virtual environment, where changes from 1K to 2K affect CS induction, but changes beyond 2K have little effect.

entities.name: LATENCY
entities.description: The time delay between a user's movement in the physical world and the corresponding change in the virtual world.

entities.name: LATENCY JITTER
entities.description: The variability or inconsistency in latency, where the time gap between physical actions and virtual reflections keeps on varying.

entities.name: HMD
entities.description: Head-mounted display, a hardware component used for semi-immersive VR experiences that can induce more cyber sickness compared to conventional monitors.

entities.name: CONVENTIONAL MONITORS
entities.description: Standard display devices used for non-immersive VR systems.

entities.name: TYPE OF DISPLAY
entities.description: A hardware factor including various screens and headsets that influences the severity of CS symptoms.

entities.name: STEREOSCOPIC 3D VIDEOS
entities.description: A type of video content used to compare experiences across different projection devices.

entities.name: FLAT SCREENS
entities.description: A type of projection device used for displaying stereoscopic 3D videos.

entities.name: PANORAMIC SCREENS
entities.description: A type of projection device used for displaying stereoscopic 3D videos.

entities.name: VR HEADSETS
entities.description: Hardware used to experience stereoscopic 3D videos, found to cause more CS than flat or panoramic screens.

entities.name: CYBERSICKNESS
entities.description: A form of discomfort and disorientation caused by virtual reality, which can be induced by longer exposure to turbulent motions, sensory mismatches, and specific locomotion factors.

entities.name: ANGULAR VELOCITY
entities.description: A measure of rotational speed; cyber sickness increases as angular velocity increases, especially around the x and y axes.

entities.name: VISUAL MOTION
entities.description: Movement perceived by the user in a virtual environment, which is linked to the occurrence of cyber sickness.

entities.name: LOCOMOTION
entities.description: The means of moving within a virtual world, encompassing how users move and how scenes transition.

entities.name: SENSORY MISMATCH
entities.description: An occurrence where users' virtual movements do not match their physical movements, resulting in discomfort and disorientation leading to cyber sickness.

entities.name: CONTROL OVER MOTION
entities.description: The degree and manner in which a user controls their movement in a virtual environment, affecting presence and cyber sickness.

entities.name: PRESENCE
entities.description: The sense of being in a virtual reality; it has a direct relationship with control over motion and an indirect relationship with cyber sickness.

entities.name: HAND-BASED MOTION CONTROL
entities.description: A type of control mechanism that leads to significantly less cyber sickness compared to whole-body motion control.

entities.name: WHOLE-BODY MOTION CONTROL
entities.description: A type of control mechanism that leads to more cyber sickness compared to hand-based motion control.

entities.name: TRANSITION
entities.description: The way scenes change and movement occurs from one field of view to another.

entities.name: TELEPORTATION
entities.description: An instantaneous transition method found to be less cyber-sickness-inducing compared to naturalistic free movement.

entities.name: NATURALISTIC FREE MOVEMENT
entities.description: Movement types such as walking, running, and jumping, which are found to be more cyber-sickness-inducing than teleportation.

entities.name: FIELD OF VIEW
entities.description: The extent to which the user's field of vision is captured by the display in a VR headset; it affects immersion and cyber sickness susceptibility.

entities.name: IMMERSION
entities.description: The sense of being absorbed in the virtual environment; it is increased by a larger field of view and decreased by an excessively narrow field of view.

entities.name: HEAD MOVEMENT
entities.description: The physical movement of the head to look for things in an environment; increased head movement due to a narrow field of view can exacerbate cyber sickness.

relationships.description: Cyber sickness increases with the increase in angular velocity.
A sensory mismatch results in discomfort and disorientation which leads to cyber sickness.
Control over motion has a direct effect on presence (more control means greater presence).
Control over motion has an indirect effect on cyber sickness through presence.
A greater sense of presence in virtual reality can lead to a lower likelihood of experiencing cyber sickness.
Hand-based motion control leads to significantly less cyber sickness.

entities.name: FOV ADJUSTMENT
entities.description: A category of strategies and techniques used by developers to adjust the Field of View (FOV) to improve user experience and reduce the chances of cybersickness.

entities.name: SYMMETRIC MASK
entities.description: A classical FOV adjustment technique where the periphery is occluded in reaction to translational and/or angular velocity; it can affect presence.

entities.name: ASYMMETRIC MASK
entities.description: An FOV adjustment technique that obscures the periphery with higher optical flow during virtual locomotion while leaving regions with lower optical flow visible; also considered an adaptive restrictor.

entities.name: SIDE RESTRICTOR
entities.description: A specific type of asymmetric mask that obscures only one side of the periphery during virtual rotation and laterally shifts the center of restriction in the direction of the turn.

entities.name: GROUND VISIBLE RESTRICTOR
entities.description: An FOV adjustment technique where the ground plane remains visible during movement.

entities.name: DYNAMIC VISUAL BLUR
entities.description: A technique to reduce the possibility of cybersickness by obscuring or reducing the clarity of certain visual regions.

entities.name: DEPTH OF FIELD BLUR
entities.description: A type of dynamic visual blur that makes use of well-known depth cues in human vision.

entities.name: PERIPHERAL BLUR
entities.description: A type of dynamic visual blur that involves dynamic non-salient region blurring.

entities.name: REST FRAMES
entities.description: Fixed elements within the virtual environment that remain stationary relative to the real world regardless of the user's movements, used to reduce cybersickness.

entities.name: INDEPENDENT VISUAL BACKGROUNDS
entities.description: Rest frames attached to the head reference frame, such as clouds, grids, and a virtual nose, which remain stationary relative to the user's movement.

entities.name: OPTICAL FLOW MANIPULATION
entities.description: A technique referring to visually mixing optical flow patterns that are in the reverse direction of virtual visual motion.

entities.name: GEOMETRICAL SIMPLIFICATION
entities.description: A technique used to reduce perceived optical flow by simplifying the geometry of the virtual environment.

entities.description: A sophisticated piece of equipment and a common metaphor for VR that integrates electronic, optical, mechanical, and audio components to place images directly in front of a user's eyes using one or two screens.

entities.name: MONOSCOPIC VIEWING
entities.description: Viewing provided by an HMD when it is using only one small screen.

entities.name: STEREOSCOPIC VIEWING
entities.description: Viewing provided by an HMD when it is using two small screens; it is more common than monoscopic viewing.

entities.name: NON-SEE-THROUGH HMD
entities.description: A category of HMD typically used in VR where the user's view of the outside world is blocked.

entities.name: OPTICAL SEE-THROUGH HMD
entities.description: A category of HMD typically used in AR where the user sees the real world through the device.

entities.name: VIDEO SEE-THROUGH HMD
entities.description: A category of HMD typically used in augmented virtuality that supports experiencing an artificial environment with real-world images.

entities.name: AUGMENTED VIRTUALITY
entities.description: An experience of an artificial or virtual environment within which some real-world images or videos appear on a real-time basis.

entities.name: WORLD FIXED DISPLAY
entities.description: A category of display that renders graphics onto surfaces that do not move with the head.

entities.name: CAVE
entities.description: A display that completely surrounds the user, representing an extreme of world-fixed displays.

entities.name: FISH TANK DISPLAY
entities.description: An early example of a world-fixed display for VR developed in 1993, showing a stereo image of a 3D scene on a fixed monitor.

entities.name: TRACKER
entities.description: An input part used to track the head position of the observer in a world-fixed display setup.

entities.name: HAPTIC DEVICES
entities.description: An input part used in the world-fixed display setup to provide tactile feedback.

relationships.description: HMDs use one screen to provide this type of viewing.

entities.name: ALIGNMENT

entities.name: FIDUCIAL MARKERS
entities.description: Reflectors or tags used to significantly aid in the registration process between real and virtual worlds.

entities.name: COMPUTER VISION
entities.description: Techniques used to perform registration even in the absence of fiducial markers.

entities.name: INTEGRATION
entities.description: The third stage of tracking where sensory output data streams arriving at regular sampling intervals are processed.

entities.name: SAMPLING INTERVAL
entities.description: Represented as delta t, it is the discrete interval at which the sensor data stream arrives.

entities.name: PERCEPTUAL DESIGN
entities.description: A design area related to the output of an XR system, intended to be designed alongside interaction design to create the best possible illusion of reality.

entities.name: PRESENCE
entities.description: The primary goal of an XR system, which is to give the user a sense of reality as if they are in the real world, achieved through an illusion of reality.

entities.name: ILLUSION OF REALITY
entities.description: The state created by designing interaction and perceptual stimuli so that the user perceives the virtual environment as their regular, familiar system.

entities.name: XR
entities.description: Extended Reality, which includes VR, AR, and MR systems, where the goal is to create a better experience through the illusion of reality.

entities.name: VR
entities.description: Virtual Reality systems where users are supposed to be totally immersed in a virtual environment, requiring a high degree of illusion of reality and presence.

entities.name: AR
entities.description: Augmented Reality systems where immersion is partial because the user can still view or experience the real world.

entities.name: MR
entities.description: Mixed Reality systems where immersion is partial because the user can still view or experience the real world.

entities.name: IMMERSION
entities.description: The feeling of being totally immersed in a virtual environment; it is achieved when the system successfully fools the user's perception into believing they are in a different world.

entities.name: PERCEPTION
entities.description: The process by which our senses and physiology work to interpret the environment; the system aims to "fool" this process to create presence.

entities.name: PERCEPTUAL SYSTEM

entities.name: PERCEPTUAL PSYCHOLOGY
entities.description: The science of understanding how the brain converts sensory stimulation into perceived phenomena, providing guidelines for building better hardware and understanding system effects on the user

entities.name: EXTENDED REALITY SYSTEMS
entities.description: Interactive systems where the goal is to explicitly extend the idea of reality, which is deeply embedded in human psychology

entities.name: SENSORY STIMULATION
entities.description: Signals from the real world that come to sensors and are converted by the brain into perceived phenomena

entities.name: PERCEIVED PHENOMENA
entities.description: The results of the brain converting sensory stimulation into internal experiences

entities.name: PRESENCE
entities.description: A state or feeling of being in a virtual environment, for which perceptual psychology can provide clues

entities.name: HARDWARE
entities.description: The physical components of a system, for which perceptual psychology provides guidelines for improvement

entities.name: VIRTUAL WORLD
entities.description: A simulated environment where questions regarding object distance, resolution, and user height are addressed

entities.name: VIRTUAL OBJECT
entities.description: A simulated item within a virtual world, where resolution needs to be high enough to avoid seeing pixels

entities.name: NAUSEATED
entities.description: A physical sensation of sickness that can be experienced by a user interacting with a system

entities.name: TIREDNESS
entities.description: A tiring effect that can vary between different experiences with a system

entities.name: SENSE ORGANS
entities.description: The biological components of the human body used to capture signals from the environment

entities.name: NEURAL PATHWAYS
entities.description: The biological connections between sense organs and the brain

entities.name: VIDEO RESOLUTION
entities.description: The amount of detail in a virtual display, used to determine if pixels are visible to the user

entities.name: FRAMES PER SECOND
entities.description: The rate at which images are updated to ensure motion is perceived as continuous

Perceptual psychology provides guidelines for building better hardware
Perceptual psychology can give clues to the overall idea of presence
Perceptual psychology is the science of how the brain converts sensory stimulation into perceived phenomena
Sensory stimulation is converted by the brain into perceived phenomena
Sense organs are connected to the brain via neural pathways
Video resolution is needed to visualize a virtual object without seeing pixels
Frames per second are necessary to perceive continuous motion in a virtual world
Users may feel nauseated when interacting with certain systems
Different experiences with a system can have different tiring effects on the user
A virtual world is a component or environment within extended reality systems

entities.name: NEURON
entities.description: A basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system, characterized by a nucleus or cell body that performs processing on inputs.

entities.name: CELL BODY
entities.description: The nucleus or main body of a neuron, which serves as a node in the brain's graph and performs processing on input signals.

entities.name: DENDRITES
entities.description: The input edges of a neuron that allow it to aggregate information from other neurons.

entities.name: AXONS
entities.description: The output edges of a neuron through which processed signals are transmitted to other neurons.

entities.name: NEURAL NETWORK
entities.description: A model of interconnection of neurons used as the original idea behind machine learning and deep learning approaches.

entities.name: SYNAPSE
entities.description: A gap between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next where electrical or chemical signals are passed.

entities.name: HIERARCHICAL PROCESSING
entities.description: A process where signals from sense organ receptors propagate through the neural network to the cerebral cortex, undergoing selective processing along the way.

entities.name: SELECTIVITY
entities.description: The property where each receptor responds to only a narrow range of stimuli across time, space, and frequency.

entities.name: CEREBRAL CORTEX
entities.description: The final destination in the brain where signals from receptors eventually reach after hierarchical processing.

entities.name: MACHINE LEARNING
entities.description: A field of study that uses the concept of neural networks to process information.

entities.name: DEEP LEARNING
entities.description: A subset of machine learning based on the principles of neural networks.

entities.name: RECEPTORS
entities.description: Sensory structures that respond to specific stimuli and initiate signal propagation through the neural network.

entities.name: GRAPH
entities.description: A mathematical structure used to represent the interconnection of neurons as nodes and edges.

entities.name: SENSES
entities.description: Inputs received from the body, including vision and proprioception, which the brain processes and combines with experience.

entities.name: PROPRIOCEPTION
entities.description: The sense of self-movement and body position, which may conflict with visual input in a virtual environment.

entities.name: LEARNING
entities.description: The process of obtaining experience over a long period of time, allowing the brain to interpret inputs in coherent and familiar ways.

entities.name: BRAIN DEVELOPMENT
entities.description: The process of learning perception and cognition over a long period of time.

entities.name: VR SYSTEM
entities.description: An immersive system where users experience a virtual world in a short span of time, potentially causing a mismatch in sensory processing.

entities.name: MISMATCH
entities.description: The conflict between data from senses and the brain's learned processing methods, often occurring when experiencing a VR system.

entities.name: CYBER SICKNESS
entities.description: A significant issue caused by sensory mismatch in a VR system, leading to symptoms like fatigue, headache, dizziness, and nausea.

entities.name: PRESENCE
entities.description: The state of feeling immersed in a virtual environment, which is compromised when the brain becomes aware of the artificiality of the experience due to sensory conflict.

entities.name: VECTION
entities.description: An illusion of self-motion where visual input reports movement or acceleration while the balance sense or proprioception reports being motionless.

entities.name: VISION
entities.description: A sensory input that, in a virtual environment, may report motion that contradicts the user's physical state.

entities.name: SENSORY CONFLICT
entities.description: A mismatch where vision tells one thing while the balance sense and proprioception tell something else, which can lead to cybersickness or compromised presence.

entities.name: BALANCE SENSE
entities.description: A sense that provides information which can conflict with vision, potentially causing sensory conflict.

entities.name: PROPRIOCEPTION
entities.description: A sense that provides information which can conflict with vision, potentially causing sensory conflict.

entities.name: CYBERSICKNESS
entities.description: A feeling of discomfort or illness that can occur when the brain is unable to adjust to sensory mismatches in an artificial world.

entities.name: PRESENCE
entities.description: The feeling of being in a different world; it can be compromised if the brain cannot adjust to sensory mismatches.

entities.name: EXTENDED REALITY
entities.description: A broad category of systems (XR) that requires careful design to balance various senses and provide an immersive experience.

entities.name: IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE
entities.description: The goal of fooling the brain into processing information in a specific way to feel as though one is in a different world.

entities.name: HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY

entities.name: PROCESS OF PERCEPTION

entities.name: VR SYSTEMS
entities.description: Systems that require an understanding of human physiology and psychology for effective design.

entities.name: LAVALLE

entities.name: LIGHT RAYS
entities.description: Electromagnetic waves that interact with surfaces through reflection, absorption, or transmission. They are the primary medium for transmitting visual information.

entities.name: REFLECTION
entities.description: The process where light rays strike a surface and bounce back without entering or penetrating the object.

entities.name: ABSORPTION
entities.description: The process where light rays are taken in by a surface rather than being reflected or transmitted.

entities.name: TRANSMISSION
entities.description: The process where light rays pass through a surface.

entities.name: COLOR PERCEPTION
entities.description: The process by which the human eye perceives the color of a point or scene, determined by the intensity of reflected light rays reaching the viewer's eye.

entities.name: INCIDENT LIGHT
entities.description: Light that falls onto a surface from a source.

entities.name: SOURCE OF LIGHT
entities.description: The origin of light rays that interact with surfaces to eventually reach the viewer's eye.

entities.name: INTENSITY OF THE RAY
entities.description: The measure of the amount of light that reaches the viewer's eye, which determines the perceived color.

entities.name: VIEWER'S EYE
entities.description: The organ of the human visual perceptual system that receives reflected light to facilitate color perception.

entities.name: SURROUNDING OBJECTS
entities.description: Objects in the environment that can reflect light indirectly toward the viewer.

entities.name: AMBIENT LIGHT
entities.description: Light in the environment that is reflected from surrounding objects and mixes with light from direct sources to reach the eye.

entities.name: VISUAL PERCEPTUAL SYSTEM
entities.description: The human biological system responsible for processing visual information, which must be understood to design good systems or identify flaws.

entities.name: NPTEL MOOC
entities.description: A massive open online course platform hosting the course on Foundations for Virtual and Augmented Reality Systems.

entities.name: FOUNDATIONS FOR VIRTUAL AND AUGMENTED REALITY SYSTEMS
entities.description: The title and subject of the course, which covers interactive systems, human factors, and extended reality systems.

entities.name: INTERACTIVE SYSTEMS
entities.description: Systems that involve user interaction, requiring consideration of user behavior and human factors to be usable and effective.

entities.name: HUMAN FACTORS
entities.description: Elements of human physiology and behavior that influence the design and overall experience of interactive systems.

entities.name: EXTENDED REALITY SYSTEMS
entities.description: A broad category of technologies including VR and AR that utilize human senses for immersive experiences.

entities.name: VISUAL SENSES
entities.description: The primary human sense used for sight, which is often the main focus of developers in extended reality systems.

entities.name: PHYSIOLOGY OF VISION
entities.description: The biological study of how the human eye and brain process visual information, used to build better display devices.

entities.name: DISPLAY DEVICES
entities.description: Hardware used to present visual information, such as headsets or cave-like surround environments.

entities.name: VIRTUAL REALITY EXPERIENCES
entities.description: Simulated environments that aim to provide immersive experiences through visual and auditory inputs.

entities.name: AUDITORY SENSES
entities.description: The human sense of hearing, which is a powerful component for providing immersive experiences in XR.

entities.name: PHYSIOLOGY OF HEARING
entities.description: The biological study of how the human auditory system processes sound, relevant for designing XR experiences.

entities.name: HUMAN AUDITORY SYSTEM
entities.description: The biological system responsible for hearing and processing audio.

entities.name: IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCES
entities.description: The feeling of being present in a virtual or augmented environment, influenced by both visual and auditory senses.

entities.name: XR
entities.description: Abbreviation for Extended Reality, encompassing technologies like VR.

entities.name: VR
entities.description: Virtual Reality, a technology more relevant for immersive experiences than other extended reality formats.

entities.name: AUDIO
entities.description: The component of sound used in virtual reality to provide an immersive experience.

entities.name: HIGH FIDELITY AUDIO EXPERIENCE
entities.description: A high-quality, realistic audio reproduction intended to improve immersion in VR.

entities.name: AUDIO RECORDING
entities.description: The process of capturing sound, speech, or non-speech sound for use in VR.

entities.name: OUTPUT GENERATION
entities.description: The reproduction of recorded audio sounds in a VR environment.

entities.name: CAVE-LIKE VERSIONS
entities.description: Surround environments surrounded by display devices where audio can provide a surround sound effect.

entities.name: HEADSET VERSION
entities.description: Wearable display versions used for VR experiences.

entities.name: NEURAL NETWORK
entities.description: A system meant for transferring neural information from one neuron to another.

entities.name: SOMATOSENSORY SYSTEM
entities.description: The biological system through which receptors receive input, transform it into a neural impulse, and transmit it via a neural network to the brain for touch perception.

entities.name: BRAIN
entities.description: The organ that processes messages from the neural network to provide touch perception and sends commands back to the body for corrective motor action.

entities.name: TOUCH PERCEPTION
entities.description: The sensory perception resulting from the brain processing messages received through the neural network from the somatosensory system.

entities.name: HAPTIC PERCEPTION
entities.description: A major part of somatosensory perception focused on the perception of the overall geometric shape of objects.

entities.name: HAPTIC EXPLORATION
entities.description: The process involving object handling or manipulation to infer the overall geometric shape of an object through haptic perception.

entities.name: LATERAL MOTION
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration used to perceive the texture of an object surface.

entities.name: TEXTURE
entities.description: The property of an object's surface perceived through lateral motion.

entities.name: PRESSURE
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration, such as pinching, used to understand the hardness of a surface.

entities.name: HARDNESS
entities.description: The property of a surface perceived through pressure.

entities.name: ENCLOSURE
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration involving putting hands around an object to perceive global shape or volume.

entities.name: GLOBAL SHAPE
entities.description: The overall geometric shape or volume of an object perceived through enclosure.

entities.name: STATIC CONTACT
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration where touching an object surface leads to temperature perception.

entities.name: TEMPERATURE
entities.description: The thermal property of an object perceived through static contact.

entities.name: UNSUPPORTED HOLDING
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration used to perceive the weight of an object.

entities.name: WEIGHT
entities.description: The heaviness of an object perceived through unsupported holding.

entities.name: CONTOUR FOLLOWING
entities.description: A type of haptic exploration where fingers move around surfaces to perceive the local shape.

entities.name: LOCAL SHAPE
entities.description: The specific shape of an object's surface perceived through contour following.

entities.description: The stage of the ISDLC where the actual code is written and the system is built based on designs.

entities.name: EMPIRICAL STUDY
entities.description: A unique activity in interactive system development involving usability testing with end users to evaluate the system's effectiveness.

entities.name: CODE TESTING
entities.description: A standard software development activity focused on testing the code, distinct from usability testing with end users.

entities.name: EXTENDED REALITY SYSTEMS
entities.description: The specific type of interactive systems being developed in this course, characterized by their need for high usability.

entities.name: USABILITY
entities.description: The quality of a system that makes it usable for the end user, which is a primary concern in interactive system development.

entities.name: DEVELOPMENT COST
entities.description: A measure of the resources, manpower, and time required to complete the project, which can escalate if loops are performed too frequently.

entities.name: TURNAROUND TIME
entities.description: The total time taken to complete the project, which is significantly affected by the frequency of iterative loops.

entities.name: CONTEXTUAL INQUIRY
entities.description: An old method, more than 30 years old, also referred to as a semi-structured interview process consisting of interviews and observations. Its primary objective is to watch and observe users perform tasks in their natural work setting or work context. It takes one to two hours if well planned and enables designers to learn about the task domain, work culture, and physical and social constraints.

entities.name: USER-CENTERED DESIGN
entities.description: A design approach where the importance of the contextual inquiry method was highlighted in 1988 (then called phenomenological research method).

entities.name: PHENOMENOLOGICAL RESEARCH METHOD
entities.description: The term used in 1988 to describe what is now known as the contextual inquiry method.

entities.name: SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEW PROCESS
entities.description: A term often used to refer to the contextual inquiry method, consisting of both interviews and observations.

entities.name: INTERVIEW
entities.description: A component of the semi-structured interview process used to ask users questions to clarify certain behaviors or activities.

entities.name: OBSERVATION
entities.description: A component of the semi-structured interview process focused on watching users perform tasks in their natural work setting.

entities.name: NATURAL WORK SETTING
entities.description: The environment or work context where users perform their tasks; it is the setting in which usability is measured.

entities.name: WORK CONTEXT
entities.description: The specific context of use where users work, which is an essential part of the definition of usability.

entities.name: USABILITY
entities.description: The quality of a system or product when measured against a specified context of use or work context.

entities.name: TASK DOMAIN
entities.description: One of the areas (along with work culture and constraints) that designers learn about through contextual inquiry to make design decisions.

entities.name: WORK CULTURE
entities.description: One of the areas that designers learn about through contextual inquiry to make design decisions.

entities.name: PHYSICAL AND SOCIAL CONSTRAINTS
entities.description: Workplace factors that designers learn about through contextual inquiry to make design decisions.

entities.name: CALENDAR APP
entities.description: A specific example of an app discussed in the lecture, intended for use by managerial staff.

entities.name: MANAGERIAL STAFF
entities.description: The assumed target group of users for the calendar app within an organization.

Contextual inquiry enables designers to learn about physical and social constraints.
The managerial staff is the target group of users for the calendar app.
Contextual inquiry is used to gather requirements to ensure a product is usable in a specific context.

entities.name: NAVIGATION
entities.description: The overall process of movement which consists of two components: locomotion (the motor component) and wayfinding.

entities.name: LOCOMOTION
entities.description: The motor component of navigation, referring to travel or movement.

entities.name: WAYFINDING
entities.description: The cognitive component of navigation referring to location awareness, ascertaining a path to a destination, and transferring spatial knowledge to the real world.

entities.name: MENTAL MODEL
entities.description: A cognitive representation of the surroundings and the overall environment that helps users locate themselves and identify paths.

entities.name: COGNITIVE MAP
entities.description: A synonym for a mental model of the surroundings used for easier navigation.

entities.name: SPATIAL KNOWLEDGE
entities.description: The information contained within a mental model or cognitive map, specifically regarding the environment.

entities.name: LANDMARK KNOWLEDGE
entities.description: Knowledge about specific landmarks in the surroundings and other places.

entities.name: PROCEDURAL KNOWLEDGE
entities.description: Knowledge of the sequence of actions required to follow a path.

entities.name: TOPOLOGICAL KNOWLEDGE
entities.description: Map-like knowledge of the overall environment.

entities.name: KNOWLEDGE BASE
entities.description: The collection of landmark, procedural, and topological knowledge that constitutes an essential part of the mental model.

entities.name: SYSTEMATIC STUDY
entities.description: A traditional method of creating a mental model by studying the map of a place.

entities.name: EXPLORATION OF REAL SPACE
entities.description: A traditional method of creating a mental model by exploring the actual physical space.

entities.name: EXPLORATION OF A COPY OF THE REAL SPACE
entities.description: A traditional method of creating a mental model by exploring a replica or model of the real space.

entities.name: USER EXPERIENCE
entities.description: The overall quality of the user's interaction with the system, which can be deteriorated if the design does not support the creation of a mental map.

entities.name: LANDMARKS
entities.description: Obvious distinct non-mobile objects positioned in a given place used to support wayfinding.

entities.name: HIGH FIDELITY APPROACH
entities.description: An approach that uses programming to create a prototype, effectively acting as actual software development on a reduced scale. It is sophisticated and requires skilled manpower programmers and expertise in programming.

entities.name: VERTICAL PROTOTYPES
entities.description: Prototypes that are primarily created using high fidelity approaches.

entities.name: HORIZONTAL PROTOTYPES
entities.description: Prototypes that are primarily meant to be created using low fidelity approaches; making them using a high fidelity approach may not make much sense.

entities.name: MEDIUM FIDELITY APPROACHES
entities.description: Approaches that are meant for both horizontal and vertical prototypes.

entities.name: LOW FIDELITY PROTOTYPES
entities.description: Prototypes that are primarily meant for horizontal prototypes.

entities.name: WIZARD OF OZ APPROACH
entities.description: An interesting technique for creating prototypes where a human subject believes they are interacting with an autonomous computer, but the computer is actually operated by an unseen human being called a wizard.

entities.name: HUMAN SUBJECT
entities.description: An individual involved in the Wizard of Oz approach who believes they are interacting with a computer and provides input via a microphone.

entities.name: COMPUTER
entities.description: A device that the human subject believes is autonomous but is actually operated by a wizard in the Wizard of Oz setup.

entities.name: WIZARD
entities.description: An unseen human being who operates the computer in the Wizard of Oz approach, responding to the human subject's inputs.

entities.name: IBM
entities.description: An organization that conducted the listening typewriter experiment in 1984 to test a speech recognition system.

entities.name: LISTENING TYPEWRITER EXPERIMENT
entities.description: An experiment conducted by IBM in 1984 to test the acceptability of a speech recognition system using the Wizard of Oz approach.

entities.name: SPEECH RECOGNITION SYSTEM
entities.description: A technology that IBM was trying to develop in 1984 but which was not yet available at the time of the experiment.

entities.name: MICROPHONE
entities.description: A device used by the human subject to speak into during the experiment.

entities.name: SPEAKER

entities.description: The first stage of the interactive system development lifecycle.

entities.name: REQUIREMENT GATHERING ANALYSIS
entities.description: The second stage of the interactive system development lifecycle, following the feasibility study.

entities.description: A stage following the design prototype evaluate cycle, comprising code design, coding, and code testing.

entities.description: The final stage of the interactive system development lifecycle.

entities.name: LOW-FIDELITY PROTOTYPE

entities.name: MESH REPRESENTATION
entities.description: The most basic form of representation for any object in a rendered scene used in computer graphics; all other representations are eventually mapped to this format at the end of the pipeline before rendering. It is typically constructed using triangles or other simple convex polygons and represented via vertex or edge lists.

entities.name: TRIANGULAR MESH
entities.description: A specific type of mesh representation constructed using triangles, used to approximate curved surfaces like a human hand.

entities.name: VERTEX LIST
entities.description: A data structure used to represent a mesh; its complexity increases with the number of polygons, making construction more difficult.

entities.name: SPLINE REPRESENTATION
entities.description: A higher-level representation for curved surfaces or curves, preferred by developers and designers to construct quality scenes; it uses several lower-degree polynomials to represent complex surfaces that cannot be handled by simple polygons.

entities.name: PARAMETRIC REPRESENTATION
entities.description: A broad category of representation that includes curve representations using splines or polynomials.

entities.name: POLYNOMIAL
entities.description: A mathematical tool used to represent curves, where the degree of the polynomial increases with the complexity of the curve, potentially increasing computation time.

entities.name: CURVED SURFACES
entities.description: Surfaces that lack intuitive polygonal representation (e.g., a human hand) and are often approximated using triangular meshes or represented via splines.

entities.name: TRADEOFF
entities.description: The balance that must be maintained between the number of polygons in a mesh (which improves approximation quality) and the complexity of the vertex list (which makes construction more difficult).

entities.name: RENDERED SCENE
entities.description: The environment or scene in which objects are displayed on a screen, requiring various representations to be converted into a mesh format.

entities.name: COMPUTER GRAPHICS

entities.name: 3D GRAPHICS PIPELINE
entities.description: A sequence of five stages involved in rendering a 3D scene, including object representation, modeling transformation, lighting, viewing pipeline, and scan conversion.

entities.name: OBJECT REPRESENTATION
entities.description: The first stage of the 3D graphics pipeline which happens in the local coordinate system and involves no computation related to pixel intensities.

entities.name: MODELING TRANSFORMATION
entities.description: The second stage of the 3D graphics pipeline where local coordinate descriptions are transformed to a world coordinate description.

entities.name: LIGHTING STAGE
entities.description: The third stage of the 3D graphics pipeline which takes place in the world coordinate reference frame.

entities.name: VIEWING PIPELINE
entities.description: The fourth stage of the 3D graphics pipeline containing several sub-stages including viewing transformation, clipping, hidden surface removal, and projection transformation.

entities.name: VIEWING TRANSFORMATION
entities.description: A sub-stage of the viewing pipeline where coordinates are transformed from a world coordinate system to a 3D view coordinate system.

entities.name: CLIPPING
entities.description: An operation taking place in the 3D view coordinate system as part of the viewing pipeline.

entities.name: HIDDEN SURFACE REMOVAL
entities.description: An operation taking place in the 3D view coordinate system as part of the viewing pipeline.

entities.name: PROJECTION TRANSFORMATION
entities.description: A sub-stage of the viewing pipeline where the 3D view coordinate is transformed to a 2D view coordinate system.

entities.name: WINDOW TO VIEWPORT TRANSFORMATION
entities.description: The process of transferring the scene description in the 2D view coordinate system to a device coordinate system.

entities.name: SCAN CONVERSION
entities.description: The fifth and final stage of the 3D graphics pipeline where the device coordinate scene description is transformed to a screen coordinate or pixel grid description.

relationships.description: The lighting model calculates intensity based on the number and properties of light sources.
Intensity mapping is the step taken to convert the output of the lighting model into a device-supported range.
Intensity mapping is required because devices have a finite range of values compared to the infinite range of the model.
An 8-bit display is provided as a specific example of a device with limited values.
The frame buffer stores the bit pattern for the values determined during intensity mapping.
A photometer is used to find the minimum value (I naught) needed for the intensity mapping calculations.
The equation used for intensity mapping is formulated based on psychophysiological properties of human perception.
The perception of relative change dictates how the successive intensity values are calculated.

entities.name: CPU
entities.description: Processors that are traditionally not designed for large-scale parallel activities and generally cannot take advantage of inherent parallelism.

entities.name: GPU
entities.description: A separate graphics card containing its own processing unit and memory elements, designed to deal with inherent parallelism in graphics operations.

entities.name: CORE
entities.description: Individual processing elements within a GPU that are capable of performing simple integer and floating-point arithmetic operations.

entities.name: STREAMING MULTIPROCESSOR UNITS
entities.description: Groups formed by multiple cores within a GPU.

entities.name: INPUT ASSEMBLERS
entities.description: Components within the GPU architecture that precede the thread execution manager.

entities.name: THREAD EXECUTION MANAGER
entities.description: A manager within the GPU that allocates tasks to different streaming multiprocessors.

entities.name: PARALLEL DATA CACHE
entities.description: A cache where the multiprocessor can produce its data.

entities.name: TEXTURE STORAGE
entities.description: An element that stores information about predefined colors, surface colors, or predetermined surface colors.

entities.name: GLOBAL MEMORY
entities.description: Memory content that can be accessed by or sent to the processing units through load and store information.

entities.name: TRIANGLES
entities.description: The fundamental shapes that scenes are assumed to be made of; surfaces are converted into triangular meshes for rendering.

entities.name: MESHES
entities.description: Representations of objects where surfaces are converted into triangular meshes for the GPU to process.

entities.name: APIS
entities.description: Interfaces in graphics libraries used to send triangle vertices to the GPU one at a time.

entities.name: MODELING TRANSFORMATIONS
entities.description: The process of simultaneously transforming multiple vertices by multiplying them by the same transformation matrix.

relationships.description: The GPU contains a large number of cores as its processing elements.

The manager allocates tasks to different streaming multiprocessors.
The GPU assumes meshes made of triangles as input and assembles vertices into triangles.
Surfaces are converted into triangular meshes.
APIs are used to send triangles from the graphics library to the GPU.
The GPU performs modeling transformations on the vertices.
The multiprocessor has a parallel data cache to produce its data.
The content of global memory is accessed by or sent to these units via load and store information.
Data can be sent to the global memory through load and store information.
The text contrasts the CPU's lack of parallelism with the GPU's design for parallel graphics operations.
